strategy.summary: Reproduce the symbolic QR hang/failure on rank-deficient symbolic matrices in sympy at commit 841185289d56 by running the PR's own test test_QR_symbolic_dependent_columns from a source checkout, which should fail or time out on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one. Sympy is pure Python, so no compiled build is needed; the test imports the checked-out tree. The Python version (3.12) is a planner choice because the evidence gives none, and no sympy version pin is documented, so the checkout itself is the pin.

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/sympy/sympy.git && cd sympy && git checkout 841185289d56
pinned_because: No sympy version constraint is documented in the README or the evidence (documented=false), and no era ceiling exists, so the planner pins the buggy commit checkout rather than a release version.
mpmath is sympy's runtime dependency; left unpinned because no constraint is stated.
Python 3.12 is chosen by the planner (python_version not given by the evidence); it is not a documented requirement.

strategy.test_command: cd sympy && timeout 600 python -m pytest sympy/matrices/tests/test_decompositions.py::test_QR_symbolic_dependent_columns -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: def test_QR_symbolic_dependent_columns(): a,b,k = Symbol('a',real=True),Symbol('b',real=True),Symbol('k',real=True); A = Matrix([[a, k*a],[b, k*b]]); Q, R = A.QRdecomposition(); assert A.rank() == 1; assert Q.cols == A.rank(); QQ = (Q.H * Q).applyfunc(simplify); assert not QQ.has(S.NaN); assert (Q*R - A).applyfunc(simplify) == zeros(2, 2)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 841185289d56: the test does not pass; it either hangs past the 600 s timeout (the reported symptom is an unfinished symbolic QR call interrupted by KeyboardInterrupt) or fails with an assertion or NaN error. Fixed revision (the PR merge): pytest reports 1 passed well inside the timeout, with A.rank()==1, Q.cols==1, no NaN in Q.H*Q, and (Q*R - A) simplifying to zeros(2,2).
strategy.numerical_probe: Under timeout, build the 5x5 issue matrix M = randMatrix(5)*x + randMatrix(5) with M[4,:] = M[1,:] + M[2,:] (seed fixed) and time M.QRdecomposition(); compare against M.to_DM(field=True).qr(), which the evidence says takes about 115 ms. Use the wall-clock time and the timeout outcome as the signal, not printed values.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: not stated by evidence (hang or assertion failure expected)
input_output_examples.expected_output: A.rank()==1 and Q.cols==A.rank(); no NaN in Q.H*Q after simplify; (Q*R - A) simplifies to zeros(2,2)

input_output_examples.input: 5x5 symbolic matrix M = randMatrix(5)*x + randMatrix(5) with M[4,:] = M[1,:] + M[2,:]; call M.QRdecomposition()
input_output_examples.buggy_output: no result; call did not finish and was interrupted with KeyboardInterrupt
input_output_examples.expected_output: decomposition completes (same matrix via M.to_DM(field=True).qr() finishes in about 115 ms)

risks: The buggy failure mode of the 2x2 test is not stated in the evidence; it may be an assertion error or NaN rather than a hang, so the timeout must be treated as a failure as well.
The hang is reported for the 5x5 matrix; the 2x2 test may run quickly on the buggy revision and fail only on an assertion, which still counts as a transition but is a different mechanism.
Symbolic simplification and .equals are sensitive to the sympy version and simplify heuristics; a different Python or sympy version could change whether the behaviour appears at all.

The reviewer notes the fix covers only _QRdecomposition_optional, not Matrix.QRdecomposition; if the test's call path goes through the DomainMatrix route instead, the bug will not be exercised and the test will not transition.
No architecture or sanitiser dependence is stated, so the platform is assumed to be an ordinary x86_64 Linux or macOS machine; the evidence does not show a platform-specific failure.
The random 5x5 matrix in the probe is not part of the project test; it is an extra check that depends on the seed and should not be used as the pass/fail criterion.
Dependency constraint for sympy is unbounded in the evidence (numerically_relevant true, documented false); the strategy relies on the checkout rather than any era-inferred version.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On revision 841185289d56 the test either does not finish within the 600 s timeout (the hang in the symbolic QR path) or raises an assertion or NaN failure at the rank, Q.cols, or (Q*R - A) check, because the unpatched _QRdecomposition_optional divides by a norm that may be symbolically zero.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the test completes quickly and all four assertions hold, so pytest reports one passed.
